name: transmembrane signal receptor
definition: A protein or complex that spans the plasma membrane, that binds to an signal molecule in the extracellular space and transduces the signal to the cytoplasm. Note that the term RECEPTOR is used in several different ways in biology, and other receptors are found in other categories.  Nuclear receptors are classified under DNA-BINDING TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR, cargo receptors are classified under MEMBRANE TRAFFICKING REGULATORY PROTEIN, ligand-gated ion channels (e.g. acetylcholine receptors) are classified under ION CHANNEL, and T-cell receptors are classified under DEFENSE/IMMUNITY PROTEIN.

name: G-protein coupled receptor
definition: Cell surface receptors that are coupled to G proteins and have 7 transmembrane spanning domains.

name: tyrosine protein kinase receptor
definition: A protein that has an extracellular ligand binding domain, a single transmembrane domain and an intracellular tyrosine kinase domain that phosphorylates protein tyrosine residues.

name: serine/threonine protein kinase receptor
definition: A protein that has an extracellular ligand binding domain, a single transmembrane domain and an intracellular serine or threonine kinase domain that phosphorylates protein serine or threonine residues.

name: histidine kinase receptor of two-component system
definition: A protein that binds to a signal and phosphorylates a response regulator protein on a histidine residue to activate it.

name: intercellular signal molecule
definition: A molecule that is secreted by one cell and received as a signal by a receptor on another cell.

name: cytokine
definition: A small protein or biological factor that is released by cells and have specific effects on cell-cell interaction, communication and behavior of other cells.  It contains interleukins, lymphokines, TNF-alpha and interferons.  Growth factors are generally not included here, although TGF-beta family members, CNTF and LIF are exceptions.

name: interleukin superfamily
definition: A cytokine produced by lymphocytes, monocytes and various other cell types and are released by cells in response to antigenic and non-antigenic stimuli. To date, there are 12 interleukins identified.  Their function is to modulate inflammation and immunity by regulating growth, mobility and differentiation of lymphoid and other cells.

name: interferon superfamily
definition: A family of glycoproteins that plays an important role in fighting viral infections by preventing viral multiplication in cells.

name: chemokine
definition: Proteins that are chemotactic for leucocytes.  They are regarded as cytokines by some people.

name: growth factor
definition: A complex family of biological factors that are produced by the body to control growth, division and maturation of various cell types.

name: neurotrophic factor
definition: A signaling molecule involved in the nutrition (or maintenance) of neural tissue.  The classic example is the nerve growth factor.

name: peptide hormone
definition: A protein or peptide that acts as a hormone.

name: neuropeptide
definition: A peptide with direct synaptic effects (peptide neurotransmitters) or indirect modulatory effects on the nervous system (peptide neuromodulators).

name: membrane-bound signaling molecule
definition: A signaling molecule that is membrane-bound and not secreted.

name: protein-binding activity modulator
definition: A protein that binds to, and modulates the activity of another protein.

name: kinase modulator
definition: A protein that directly interacts with a kinase and affects its activity.

name: kinase activator
definition: A protein that directly interacts with a kinase and activates or enhance its activity.

name: kinase inhibitor
definition: A protein that directly interacts with a kinase and inhibits its activity.

name: phosphatase modulator
definition: A protein that directly interacts with a phosphatase and affects its activity.

name: phosphatase activator
definition: A protein that directly interacts with a phosphatase and activates or enhance its activity.

name: phosphatase inhibitor
definition: A protein that directly interacts with a phosphatase and inhibits its activity.

name: G-protein
definition: A GTP-binding protein that is either part of the heterotrimeric G protein class or of the small GTP-binding class.

name: heterotrimeric G-protein
definition: the heterotrimeric G proteins that associate with receptors of the seven transmembrane domain superfamily and are involved in signal transduction.

name: small GTPase
definition: The small G proteins are a diverse group of monomeric GTPases that include ras, rab, rac and rho and that play an important part in regulating many intracellular processes including cytoskeletal organization and secretion.

name: G-protein modulator
definition: A protein that directly interacts with a G-protein and affects its activity.

name: guanyl-nucleotide exchange factor
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the exchange of GDP and GTP in a G-protein.

name: GTPase-activating protein
definition: A protein that binds to a GTPase to stimulate its GTPase activity, converting it to the GDP-bound form.

name: protease inhibitor
definition: Compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of proteases.

name: calcium-binding protein
definition: A protein with the primary function of binding to calcium, either to store calcium or to participate in calcium cell signalling pathways by modulating its function after binding to Ca2+.

name: calmodulin-related
definition: A calcium binding protein that are similar to calmodulin and are called EF hand proteins.

name: gene-specific transcriptional regulator
definition: A protein that regulates transcription of a set of specific genes.

name: DNA-binding transcription factor
definition: A protein required for the regulation of RNA polymerase by specific regulatory sequences in or near a gene.

name: zinc finger transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor containing zinc finger domain(s), which is composed of conserved cysteines and histidines co-ordinate with zinc ion(s).  Examples of zinc finger domains are C2H2 zinc finger, C3HC4 zinc finger, CHC2 zinc finger, etc.

name: C4 zinc finger nuclear receptor
definition: A receptor of steroid hormones that traverses the nuclear membrane to activate transcription.

name: C2H2 zinc finger transcription factor
definition: A zinc-coordinating transcription factor with C2H2 zinc finger DNA binding domains.

name: C6 zinc finger transcription factor
definition: A zinc-coordinating transcription factor with a C6 zinc finger DNA binding domain.

name: HMG box transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor containing high mobility group protein (HMG) box.

name: basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor containing helix-loop-helix (HLH) DNA binding domain.

name: basic leucine zipper transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor that contains the basic leucine zipper (bZIP) domain, where one part of the domain contains a region that mediates sequence specific DNA binding properties and the leucine zipper that is required for the dimerization of two DNA binding regions.

name: CREB-related transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor that regulates transcription by binding to the cyclic AMP response element (CRE).

name: helix-turn-helix transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor that has the helix-turn-helix (HTH) domain, a major DNA-binding structural motif composed of two _ helices joined by a short strand of amino acids.

name: homeodomain transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor containing the homeobox domain. It is usually involved in the control of gene expression during morphogenesis and development.

name: paired box transcription factor
definition: A tissue specific transcription factor that contains a paired domain and usually a partial or complete homeodomain.

name: Lambda repressor-like transcription factor
definition: A helix-turn-helix transcription factor with a similar DNA binding domain fold to the Lambda repressor in bacteria.

name: winged helix/forkhead transcription factor
definition: A helix-turn-helix transcription factor with a forkhead DNA binding domain.

name: Trp repressor-like transcription factor
definition: A helix-turn-helix transcription factor with a similar DNA binding domain fold to the Trp repressor in bacteria.

name: Tet repressor-like transcription factor
definition: A helix-turn-helix transcription factor with a similar DNA binding domain fold to the Tet repressor in bacteria.

name: Sigma factor
definition: A specific DNA sequence binding transcription initiation factor.

name: MADS box transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor with a MADS box DNA binding domain.

name: immunoglobulin fold transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor with a DNA binding domain with a fold similar to immunoglobulins.

name: Rel homology transcription factor
definition: An immunoglobulin fold transcription factor with a Rel homology region (RHR) DNA binding domain.

name: P53-like transcription factor
definition: An immunoglobulin fold transcription factor with a DNA binding domain with a fold similar to p53.

name: Runt transcription factor
definition: An immunoglobulin fold transcription factor with a Runt domain.

name: SMAD-like transcription factor
definition: A transcription factor with a similar DNA binding domain alpha/beta fold to the SMAD (related to Drosophila “mothers against decapentaplegic” gene product) proteins.

name: transcription cofactor
definition: A protein that has no DNA binding domains, but regulates transcription by binding to other transcription factors.

name: DNA metabolism protein
definition: A protein that acts on DNA to modify it either topologically (e.g. bending), its base-pairing, or covalently.

name: primase
definition: The enzyme that polymerizes ribonucleoside triphosphates to form oligoribonucleotides in a 5 prime to 3 prime direction.

name: DNA-directed DNA polymerase
definition: An enzyme involved in template directed synthesis of DNA from deoxyribonucleotide triphosphates.

name: DNA polymerase processivity factor
definition: A protein that enhances the processivity of DNA polymerase.

name: replication origin binding protein
definition: A protein that binds specifically to the origin of replication.

name: DNA photolyase
definition: A DNA repair enzyme that recognizes and monomerizes pyrimidine dimers using visible light.

name: DNA ligase
definition: An enzyme that seals nicks in one strand of double stranded DNA, by forming a phosphodiester linkage between a free 3 prime OH and 5 prime phosphate groups of two adjacent nucleotide residues.

name: DNA glycosylase
definition: An enzyme that recognizes altered bases in DNA and catalyzes their removal by cleaving the glycosidic bond between the base and the deoxyribose sugar.

name: DNA methyltransferase
definition: An enzyme that methylates specific bases in DNA.

name: DNA topoisomerase
definition: Enzymes that change the degree of supercoiling in DNA by cutting one or both strands.

name: damaged DNA-binding protein
definition: A protein that binds specifically to damaged DNA.

name: DNA strand-pairing protein
definition: An enzyme that pairs complementary DNA molecules during genetic recombination.

name: exodeoxyribonuclease
definition: An enzyme that cleaves DNA sequentially from the free ends of a linear nucleic acid substrate.

name: endodeoxyribonuclease
definition: One of a large group of enzymes that cleaves DNA at an internal position in the chain.

name: DNA helicase
definition: An enzyme that promotes the unwinding of duplex DNA.

name: RNA metabolism protein
definition: A protein that binds RNA and is involved in RNA processing or metabolism.

name: DNA-directed RNA polymerase
definition: An enzyme that polymerizes ribonucleotides using a DNA template.  Factors involved in REGULATING this process are categorized under TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR.

name: RNA methyltransferase
definition: An enzyme that methylates specific bases in RNA.

name: RNA processing factor
definition: A factor involved in RNA processing, including capping, polyadenylation and splicing.

name: mRNA capping factor
definition: A factor involved in mRNA capping.

name: mRNA polyadenylation factor
definition: A factor involved in mRNA polyadenylation.

name: RNA splicing factor
definition: A factor involved in RNA splicing.

name: exoribonuclease
definition: An enzyme that cleaves RNA sequentially from the free ends of a linear nucleic acid substrate.

name: endoribonuclease
definition: One of a large group of enzymes that cleaves RNA at an internal position in the chain.

name: RNA helicase
definition: An enzyme that promotes the unwinding of RNA.

name: general transcription factor
definition: A protein involved in the general (non-gene-specific) transcription process.

name: translational protein
definition: A protein involved in translation of mRNA to protein.

name: ribosomal protein
definition: A protein that comprises part of the ribosome.

name: translation factor
definition: A non-ribosomal protein involved in translation initiation, elongation or termination.

name: translation initiation factor
definition: A non-ribosomal protein involved in translation initiation.

name: translation elongation factor
definition: A non-ribosomal protein involved in translation elongation.

name: translation release factor
definition: A non-ribosomal protein involved in translation release.

name: aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase
definition: Any of the group of ligases that catalyzes the ATP-driven formation of a bond between an amino acid and a tRNA.   Also called aminoacyl-tRNA ligase.

name: transporter
definition: A class of transmembrane proteins that allows substances to cross plasma membranes far faster than would be possible by diffusion alone.

name: ion channel
definition: A protein creating a highly selective transmembrane pore that presents a hydrophilic channel for specific ions to cross a lipid bilayer.

name: ligand-gated ion channel
definition: A transmembrane ion channel whose permeability is increased by the binding of a specific ligand.

name: voltage-gated ion channel
definition: A transmembrane ion channel whose permeability to ions is sensitive to the transmembrane potential difference.

name: primary active transporter
definition: A major class of transporters that transport by using a primary energy source (e.g. ATP hydrolysis or decarboxylation) to drive transport against a concentration gradient.

name: ATP synthase
definition: An integral membrane protein that transport protons across a membrane against a concentration gradient. This transport is driven by hydrolysis of ATP by hydrogen-transporting ATP synthase.

name: ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter
definition: A superfamily of oligopeptide permease proteins responsible for transporting a wide range of substrates across membranes.

name: secondary carrier transporter
definition: A major class of transport proteins that transport via facilitated diffusion or by transport of more than one species in either one direction (symporter) or opposite directions (antiporter).

name: amino acid transporter
definition: A class of transport proteins that transport amino acid across the plasma membrane.

name: mitochondrial carrier protein
definition: A protein that is located in the inner membrane of mitochondria and transports small molecules or protons within the membrane bilayer.

name: transfer/carrier protein
definition: Proteins that carry specific substances in the blood or in the cell. They usually are not involved in transmembrane transport.

name: apolipoprotein
definition: The protein component of serum lipoproteins.

name: globin
definition: The polypeptide moiety of hemoglobin.  Both hemaglobin and myoblogin belong to this category.

name: cell adhesion molecule
definition: A protein that mediates cell-to-cell adhesion.

name: immunoglobulin superfamily cell adhesion molecule
definition: Immunoglobulin superfamily CAMs (IgSF CAMs) are either homophilic or heterophilic and bind integrins or different IgSF CAMs.  Examples are NCAMs, ICAMs, and PECAM.

name: cadherin
definition: An integral membrane protein involved in calcium dependent cell adhesion.

name: integrin
definition: The integrins are a family of heterophilic CAMs that bind IgSF CAMs or the extracellular matrix. They are heterodimers, consisting in two noncovalently-linked subunits, called alpha and beta

name: cytoskeletal protein
definition: Major constituent of the cytoskeleton found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells. They form a flexible framework for the cell, provide attachment points for organelles and formed bodies, and make communication between parts of the cell possible.

name: actin or actin-binding cytoskeletal protein
definition: A protein that is either actin itself or binds to actin to form the cytoskeleton of the cell.

name: actin and actin related protein
definition: An actin protein or a protein that is related to actin.

name: non-motor actin binding protein
definition: An actin binding protein that is not involved in motor function.

name: actin binding motor protein
definition: A family of motor ATPases that interact with F actin filaments.  A typical member in this category is myosin.

name: microtubule or microtubule-binding cytoskeletal protein
definition: A protein that is either microtubule itself or binds to microtubule to form the cytoskeleton of the cell.

name: tubulin
definition: An abundant cytoplasmic protein in the microtubule family that is involved in nucleation of microtubule assembly during the cell cycle.

name: non-motor microtubule binding protein
definition: A nonmotor protein that binds to microtubule cytoskeletal protein.

name: microtubule binding motor protein
definition: A family of motor proteins that are responsible for moving vesicles and particles along the microtubule.  Typical examples are dynein and kinesin.

name: intermediate filament
definition: A cytoplasmic filament protein so named originally because their diameter (nominally 10 nm) in muscle cells was intermediate between thick and thin filaments.

name: intermediate filament binding protein
definition: A protein that binds to intermediate filament.

name: extracellular matrix protein
definition: A protein that is produced and secreted by cells and forms an intricate extracellular meshwork in which cells are embedded to construct tissues.

name: extracellular matrix structural protein
definition: A protein that forms the structural backbone of  extracellular matrix in which cells are embedded to construct tissues.

name: extracellular matrix glycoprotein
definition: An extracellular matrix protein which is conjugated with one or more covalently linked carbohydrate residues.

name: extracellular matrix linker protein
definition: An extracellular matrix protein which has multiple domains that confer the ability to interact with many extracellular substances.

name: cell junction protein
definition: Proteins that form specialized junctions between cells.

name: gap junction
definition: A protein that creates a gap junction.  A gap junction is a junction between two cells consisting of many pores that allow the passage of molecules.

name: tight junction
definition: A tight junction is a specialized intercellular junction in which the two plasma membranes are separated by only 1-2nm.  It is found near the apical surface of cells in simple epithelia, and forms a sealing gasket around the cell.

name: metabolite interconversion enzyme
definition: An enzyme that acts to convert one small molecule to another.  This class includes all enzymes except those that act on DNA, RNA or a protein.

name: oxidoreductase
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes a redox reaction.

name: oxygenase
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the incorporation of molecular oxygen into organic substrates.

name: peroxidase
definition: A heme enzyme that catalyzes reduction of hydrogen peroxide by a substrate that loses two hydrogen atoms.

name: dehydrogenase
definition: An enzyme that oxidizes a substrate by transferring hydrogen to an acceptor that is either NAD/NADP or a flavin enzyme.

name: reductase
definition: An enzyme that introduces an electron into its substrate from an electron donor.  The reaction is usually coupled with an oxidation reaction.

name: oxidase
definition: An enzyme that removes an electron from its substrate to an electron acceptor.  The reaction is usually coupled with a reduction reaction.

name: hydroxylase
definition: A type of enzyme that adds -OH groups to its substrate during hydroxylation by attaching oxygen atoms to it.

name: transferase
definition: Enzymes transferring a group from one compound (donor) to another compound (acceptor).

name: kinase
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate from ATP to a second substrate (EC2.7).

name: carbohydrate kinase
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the phosphorylation of a sugar or carbohydrate.

name: nucleotide kinase
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the phosphorylation of a nucleotide.

name: amino acid kinase
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the phosphorylation of an amino acid.

name: nucleotidyltransferase
definition: A class of enzymes that transfers nucleotidyl residues.

name: methyltransferase
definition: A class of enzymes that transfers methyl groups (EC2.1).

name: transketolase
definition: Together with transaldolase, links the pentose phosphate pathway with glycolysis by converting pentoses to hexoses.

name: transaldolase
definition: Together with transketolase, links the pentose phosphate pathway with glycolysis by converting pentoses to hexoses.

name: acetyltransferase
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of an acetyl group, usually from acetyl coenzyme A, to another compound.

name: glycosyltransferase
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a sugar (monosaccharide) unit from a sugar nucleotide derivative to a sugar or amino acid acceptor (EC2.4).

name: transaminase
definition: A subclass of enzymes that catalyze the transfer of an amino group from a donor (generally an amino acid) to an acceptor (generally 2 keto acid) in a cyclic process using pyridoxal phosphate as a cofactor (EC2.6).

name: acyltransferase
definition: An enzyme of the transferase class that catalyzes the transfer of an acyl group from a donor (often the corresponding acyl coenzyme A derivative) to an acceptor compound (EC2.3).

name: hydrolase
definition: Enzymes catalyzing hydrolysis of a variety of bonds, such as esters, glycosides, or peptides.

name: lipase
definition: Enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of fats (monoglycerides, diglycerides and triglycerides) to glycerol and fatty acids. Calcium ions are usually required.

name: phospholipase
definition: Enzymes that hydrolyze ester bonds in phospholipids. They comprise two types: aliphatic esterases (phospholipase A1, A2 and B) that release fatty acids, and phosphodiesterases (types C and D) that release diacyl glycerol or phosphatidic acid respectively.

name: esterase
definition: Enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of organic esters to release an alcohol or thiol and acid.

name: phosphodiesterase
definition: Enzymes that cleave phosphodiesters to give a phosphomonoester and a free hydroxyl group.

name: phosphatase
definition: An enzyme that hydrolyzes phosphomonoesters.

name: carbohydrate phosphatase
definition: An enzyme that hydrolyzes phosphomonoesters in carbohydrate.

name: nucleotide phosphatase
definition: An enzyme that hydrolyzes phosphomonoesters in nucleotides.

name: amylase
definition: A group of amylolytic enzymes that cleave starch, glycogen, and related alpha-1,4-glucans.

name: deacetylase
definition: An enzyme that removes acetate from a molecule.

name: deaminase
definition: An enzyme that removes amino groups from compounds, producing ammonia in the process.

name: pyrophosphatase
definition: Enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of diphosphate bonds, chiefly in nucleoside di- and triphosphates. They may liberate either a mono- or diphosphate.

name: glycosidase
definition: An enzyme that breaks up and degrades complex sugar subunits of a polysaccharide such as starch or sucrose into simple ones, such as glucose or fructose.

name: glucosidase
definition: Enzymes that hydrolyze o-glucosyl-compounds.

name: galactosidase
definition: One of a class of enzymes that cuts the glycosidic bond between the sugar galactose and another sugar molecule (of a different type than galactose).

name: lyase
definition: Enzymes that either strip a group from a molecule to form a double bond or add a group to a double bond.

name: aldolase
definition: An enzyme that catalyses an aldol condensation, i.e. a base-catalyzed addition reaction of two aldehydes or an aldehyde and a ketone to form an aldol (an organic compound that is both an aldehyde and an alcohol) and its reversal.

name: dehydratase
definition: Enzymes that remove hydroxyl groups from compounds, producing water in the process.

name: hydratase
definition: Enzymes that add hydroxyl groups to compounds, using water in the process.

name: decarboxylase
definition: Enzymes that remove carboxyl groups from compounds, producing carbonate in the process.

name: cyclase
definition: Enzymes responsible for converting a linear molecule into a cyclic molecule, such as a nucleoside triphosphate to cyclic nucleoside monophosphate.

name: adenylate cyclase
definition: An enzyme that is responsible for catalyzing the synthesis of adenosine 3', 5' cyclic monophosphate from adenosine 5' triphosphate.

name: guanylate cyclase
definition: An enzyme that is responsible for catalyzing the synthesis of guanosine 3', 5' cyclic monophosphate from guanosine 5' triphosphate.

name: isomerase
definition: A class of enzymes that catalyze geometric or structural changes within a molecule to form a single product. The reactions do not involve a net change in the concentrations of compounds other than the substrate and the product.

name: epimerase/racemase
definition: Enzymes that catalyze inversion of the configuration around an asymmetric carbon in a substrate having one (racemase) or more (epimerase) center(s) of asymmetry (EC5.1).

name: mutase
definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the switching of functional groups on a molecule.

name: ligase
definition: A class of enzymes that catalyze the formation of a bond between two substrate molecules, coupled with the hydrolysis of a pyrophosphate bond in ATP or a similar energy donor.

name: defense/immunity protein
definition: A specific protein substance that is produced to take part in various defense and immune responses of the body.

name: complement component
definition: One of 20 distinct serum proteins that is the effector of immune cytolysis.

name: major histocompatibility complex protein
definition: A set of plasmalemmal glycoproteins on the surface of all nucleated cells that are crucial for T-cell recognition of antigens.  They are the major antigens responsible for tissue recognition. There are two classes of histocompatibility antigens: Class I and Class II.

name: antimicrobial response protein
definition: A peptide, e.g. defensin, that has antimicrobial function.

name: immunoglobulin
definition: A specific protein substance that is produced by plasma cells to aid in fighting infection by taking part in various immune responses of the body to bacteria or foreign substances.

name: immunoglobulin receptor superfamily
definition: A receptor that contains an immunoglobulin domain.  It is often involved in immune response.  Some of the common members in this category are T cell receptors and IgG receptors.

name: membrane traffic protein
definition: A protein that is located on an intracellular vesicle membrane, and is responsible for the docking or fusion of the vesicle to the cytoplasma membrane.

name: vesicle coat protein
definition: A protein that is found in the secretory vesicle membrane.

name: SNARE protein
definition: A protein responsible for fusion of vesicle membrane and the plasma membrane, so as to release the content of the vesicle to the extracellular environment.

name: membrane trafficking regulatory protein
definition: A protein that regulates the release of secretory vesicle.

name: chaperone
definition: A cytoplasmic protein that binds to nascent or unfolded polypeptides and ensures correct folding or transport.

name: chaperonin
definition: Subset of chaperone proteins found in prokaryotes, mitochondria and plastids.

name: Hsp60 family chaperone
definition: Hsp60 (GroEL/GroES complex in E. coli) is a mitochondrial chaperonin that is typically held responsible for the transportation and refolding of proteins from the cytoplasm into the mitochondrial matrix. In addition to its role as a heat shock protein, HSP60 functions as a chaperonin to assist in folding linear amino acid chains into their respective three-dimensional structure.

name: Hsp70 family chaperone
definition: Widely distributed group of conserved heat-shock proteins of average weight 70 kD (DnaK in E. coli). Possess ATP binding domains and may be involved in protein folding or export.

name: Hsp90 family chaperone
definition: Widely distributed group of conserved heat-shock proteins of average weight 90 kD (HtpG in E. coli). Exact function unknown, but are found associated with steroid hormone receptors and tyrosine kinase oncogene products. May also bind actin and tubulin.

name: Hsp100 family chaperone
definition: Hsp100 (Clp family in E. coli) proteins form large hexameric structures with unfoldase activity in the presence of ATP. These proteins are thought to function as chaperones by processively threading client proteins through a small 2 nm pore, thereby giving each client protein a second chance to fold.

name: viral or transposable element protein
definition: A protein specific to a virus, endogenous protein of viral origin, or transposable element.

name: reverse transcriptase
definition: A DNA polymerase that uses RNA as a template.

name: scaffold/adaptor protein
definition: An intracellular protein that interacts with one or more other proteins, serving as either a regulator or adaptor for one protein to act on another, or to localize a protein to a specific location in the cell.

name: structural protein
definition: Extracellular proteins that form a structure for an organ or organism, such as the cuticle.

name: myelin protein
definition: Proteins found in the myelin sheath, which wraps around the nerve fibers serving as an insulator in both central and peripheral nervous system.

name: surfactant
definition: A surface active agent, the best known example of which is the lung surfactant that renders the alveolar surfaces hydrophobic and prevents the lung filling with water by capillary action.

name: storage protein
definition: A protein that stores nutrients.  Usually these are serum or milk proteins.

name: protein modifying enzyme
definition: A protein that directly covalently modifies another protein, e.g. a protein kinase or protease. Note that this category excludes receptor protein kinases (found under TRANSMEMBRANE SIGNAL RECEPTOR), and histone-modifying enzymes (found under CHROMATIN-REGULATING PROTEIN).

name: non-receptor tyrosine protein kinase
definition: A soluble protein catalyzing transfer of phosphate from ATP to tyrosine residue.

name: non-receptor serine/threonine protein kinase
definition: A soluble protein catalyzing transfer of phosphate from ATP to serine or threonine residue.

name: protein phosphatase
definition: An enzyme that hydrolyzes phosphomonoesters in proteins.

name: protease
definition: Enzymes that hydrolyze peptide bonds.

name: metalloprotease
definition: A protease whose catalytic activity requires a transition metal.

name: cysteine protease
definition: Peptide hydrolases that have a creaction mechanism in which an active site cysteine acts as a nucleophile.

name: serine protease
definition: An endoprotease that has a reaction mechanism in which an active site serine acts as a nucleophile.

name: aspartic protease
definition: Peptide hydrolases that have two aspartyl residues in the active site.

name: ubiquitin-protein ligase
definition: An enzyme that couples ubiquitin to protein by a peptide bond between the C-terminal glycine of ubiquitin and a-amino groups of lysine residues in the protein.

name: chromatin/chromatin-binding, or -regulatory protein
definition: A protein that either binds DNA to comprise chromatin or which binds chromatin.

name: histone
definition: A protein found in the nuclei of all eukaryotic cells where it is complexed to DNA to form chromatin.

name: histone modifying enzyme
definition: A protein that directly covalently modifies a histone, to affect chromatin structure.

name: centromere DNA-binding protein
definition: A protein that binds specifically to centromeric DNA.
